subject: Proposal: Converting quarterly billing to annual prepay — credit & ramp structure
body:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@acmehealth.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Javier Soto <javier.soto@acmehealth.com>, Marco Diaz <cfo@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Billing cadence change — interest in annual prepay and multi-year pricing

Hi Sergio,

Quick note from our side after the QBR: Acme is evaluating moving our Redwood usage from quarterly invoices to an annual prepay structure for 2026 to simplify forecasting. We run a ramp over the year (low in Q1, higher in Q3/Q4) and want to understand:

- Typical term discounts you offer for 1yr vs 2yr prepay (and any step-downs if usage ramps)
- How you handle credits for unused committed spend during a calendar-year ramp
- Whether Redwood will allow a conversion credit for the remaining balance if we move mid-contract from monthly/quarterly to annual prepay

Budget team asked for an example concession structure and a sample SOW to show procurement. Can you send something we can attach to the internal approval packet?

Thanks — Elena
Director, Product Operations
Acme Health

---
From: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Javier Soto <javier.soto@acmehealth.com>, Marco Diaz <cfo@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Billing cadence change — interest in annual prepay and multi-year pricing

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. High level answer first, then a concrete proposal attached.

Short answers:
- 1yr prepay: standard single-year term discount is 12% off list on token units for the committed volume.
- 2yr prepay: we typically provide 18% in year 1 and 22% in year 2 (accelerated discounting) for multi-year commitments.
- Ramp adjustments: we apply a scheduled ramp credit model — if your committed profile is 60/80/120/140 (by quarter) and actual usage is lower in early quarters, we give a quarterly true-up credit applied to your invoice/next renewal, not cash refunds.
- Mid-contract conversion credit: yes, we can credit the unused portion of pre-paid spend toward a new annual prepay, calculated pro-rata by remaining term and adjusted for realized usage.

Concrete attachment: I attached "RW-Acme-Prepay-credits-v1.xlsx" — it includes two lanes: a 12-month conversion (monthly -> annual prepay) with a one-time conversion credit equal to 15% of remaining paid-but-unused balance, and a 24-month option (if you sign for 2 years) that layers an upfront credit and an additional 3% list discount in year 2. The spreadsheet models three ramp profiles (conservative, expected, aggressive).

Next steps I suggest:
1) I’ll loop in Marissa (Sales Ops) to prepare a redlineable SOW and final pricing table.
2) If legal procurement needs it, we can provide a template SOW + a sample DocuSign link for signature.
3) If you want, I can schedule a 30-min call with our finance lead to walk through the credit calc.

If that structure sounds workable, say the word and I’ll send an updated SOW + internal approval packet.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com | +1 415-555-6210

Attachment: RW-Acme-Prepay-credits-v1.xlsx (Excel workbook, 3 tabs: Summary, Ramp-models, Calc)

---
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Nov 2025 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Billing cadence change — SOW + concession guardrails

Sergio — quick internal sync.

Notes / guardrails for commercial:
- Approval: For a 1yr prepay with a one-time conversion credit up to 15% of unused balance, Sales Ops can approve up to $75k in total concessions. Anything above requires Finance Director (Vivek) sign-off.
- 2yr deals where combined credits + add-on discounts exceed 20% of ARR need Legal & RevOps review for revenue recognition impacts. Loop Dev for contract language.
- Credit mechanics: credits are issued as account-level credit notes applied to the next invoice or renewal. We should avoid cash-back.
- SOW: include an explicit schedule showing committed units by quarter and the true-up cadence (quarterly).

I attached a draft SOW stub (SOW-draft-Acme-2025.pdf) and a quick pricing table. Sergio — if you confirm the numbers I’ll produce a redlineable SOW and the DocuSign envelope.

Marissa Cole
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachment: SOW-draft-Acme-2025.pdf

---
From: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@acmehealth.com>, Javier Soto <javier.soto@acmehealth.com>, Marco Diaz <cfo@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Nov 2025 14:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Billing cadence change — interest in annual prepay and multi-year pricing

Elena — looping you back in with the version we intend to send to Procurement. Key points in the attached:
- Option A (12-month conversion): Convert remaining 2025 quarterly balance to a 12-month annual prepay for 2026. We'll apply a one-time conversion credit = 15% of the unused quarterly prepay balance. Committed discount = 12% off list on committed units.
- Option B (24-month): Sign a 24-month prepay with an upfront conversion credit of 18% of remaining balance plus an incremental 3% list discount applied in year 2.
- True-up cadence: quarterly. Credits applied as account credits, not cash refunds.
- PO / invoicing: Redwood issues one annual invoice for prepay. We accept PO and standard Net30 terms for services invoiced.

Requested: Can Procurement send a short table with your expected committed units per quarter (even a single row: conservative/expected/aggressive) so we can lock the credit numbers into the SOW? Once we have that, Marissa will publish the DocuSign link.

If Procurement confirms the table by EOD Monday I’ll aim to have DocuSign ready by Wednesday.

Best — Sergio

---
From: Javier Soto <javier.soto@acmehealth.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Billing cadence change — interest in annual prepay and multi-year pricing

Sergio/Elena — attaching Acme’s committed units by quarter (3 profiles) per your request. We prefer Option B if the PO workflow and year-2 discount are guaranteed. Procurement asks to confirm: 1) whether the conversion credit reduces initial recognized revenue or whether it is shown as an account credit (Procurement wants a line-item credit on invoice), and 2) whether we can get the DocuSign envelope with the SOW + Exhibit A (committed units) to start routing for internal approvals.

Attachment: Acme-Committed-Profile-2026.csv

Regards,
Javier Soto
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Health

---
From: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Billing cadence change — revenue recognition & invoice presentation

Marissa / Sergio / Vivek — on the accounting side:
- Presentation: conversion credits should be shown on the invoice as an account-level credit line (not as a cash refund). That preserves the invoice as a gross bill with an applied credit.
- Revenue recognition: credits do reduce recognized revenue if they are effectively delivered as performance adjustments. Recommend we classify the one-time conversion credit as a contra-revenue adjustment tied to the contract; RevOps should document in the SOW how credits will be applied and in which reporting period.
- PO flow: DocuSign + PO is fine. For 2yr deals we need a short clause on early termination (prorated repayment of conversion credit) — Dev can draft a paragraph.

I’ll draft the revenue language and a short early-termination clause and push to the SOW.

Dev Patel
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

---
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@acmehealth.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Javier Soto <javier.soto@acmehealth.com>, Marco Diaz <cfo@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Billing cadence change — interest in annual prepay and multi-year pricing

Thanks — this is helpful and matches what the budget committee wanted to see. We’ll move forward with Option B (24-month) pending the SOW + early-termination language. Procurement will route the PO once DocuSign is available.

Please include a short example in the SOW of how the early-termination repayment would be calculated (e.g., pro-rata unused credits less a 10% administrative margin). If you can give us the DocuSign by Wednesday that would be great.

Elena Ruiz
Director, Product Operations
Acme Health
